context: You’re at the edge of the Steeps Strake Market talking to a street hawker who sells sensational broadsheets for the local Gazette. These sellers habitually play up emotion—shifting between theatrical sorrow (pretending to cry or beg) and bluster—to coax sales, and the papers trade in local gossip (reports like Stelmane’s death circulate widely). The hawker may already recognize the player from a recent edition and will react strongly if the player appears on the front page, pressing a sale or quickly handing over a copy to avoid trouble. Nearby companions can sometimes interject, and the vendor will insist he merely hawks the Gazette (sometimes claiming the paper has the Steel Watch’s protection) while demanding the usual fee.
